product: Power control solutions. Grid (Gridtec) sells STATCOM systems, metal-enclosed capacitor banks, shunt reactors, filters and power and distribution transformers through Comtrafo, Neeltran, NEPSI and NWL. Wind (Windtec) supplies turbine electrical control systems and licenses designs. Marine sells naval ship protection systems. Superconductor Amperium sales remain limited.
demand: Strong on reported metrics. Q1 FY26 orders exceeded 130 million usd, the 12-month backlog exceeded 300 million and total backlog exceeded 400 million. Q1 order mix was about one third materials, about 30 pct traditional energy, roughly 10 pct each renewables, utility and other industrial, and just under 5 pct military.
pricing_power: Mixed. Bundling complementary products raises content per project about fivefold, per the CEO on the 25 million mining order, and reduces customer complexity, but Q1 gross margin fell to 26.3 pct. Pricing is not fully offsetting mix and input and labor cost pressure in the current quarter.
competition: The company risk factor states our products face competition, which could limit our ability to acquire or retain customers. Competitors are large global electrical equipment and power quality suppliers, and the filing warns that industry consolidation could result in more powerful competitors and fewer customers. No named competitor set was disclosed.
team: Chairman, President and CEO Daniel P. McGahn; Chief Financial Officer John Kosiba; Director of Communications Nicol Golez. Seven directors were elected at the July 31 2026 annual meeting, then Barbara G. Littlefield resigned effective September 18 2026. Auditor RSM US LLP was ratified. About 1,195 employees.
market_strategy: Sell more content per project by bundling STATCOM, capacitor banks, reactors, transformers, switchgear and protection into turnkey utility and materials projects, which the CEO says can multiply revenue per project about fivefold. Diversify across mining, semiconductors, traditional energy, utility, military and renewables, expand Brazil and Latin America capacity, and pursue data center and AI grid demand.
bull: Q1 FY26 revenue 94.1M up 30 pct, record orders over 130M, total backlog over 400M, cash 153.1M; CEO says bundling lifts content per project about fivefold.
bear: Gross margin fell to 26.3 pct from 33.8 pct; Q1 revenue pulled forward; Q2 GAAP net income guided to about 1M; stock fell 50.4 pct over 52 weeks; Roth cut target to 55.
falsifier: Q2 FY26 results (estimated 2026-11-04) showing revenue below 85M or gross margin still near 26 pct would prove the bull case wrong.
web_what_changed: Aug 4-5 2026 Q1 FY26 results (quarter ended Jun 30 2026): revenue 94.1M usd up 30 pct, record orders over 130M, 12-month backlog over 300M, total backlog over 400M, cash 153.1M, operating cash flow 16M. Late July: record 25M North American utility mining turnkey order. Jul 31 2026 annual meeting. Aug 10 Roth MKM cut target 58 to 55. Sep 17 2026 director Barbara Littlefield resigned.
web_not_known_yesterday: Nothing new from the company: no press release, 8-K or 10-Q since the Sep 21 2026 board resignation filing. The only fresh item is a Sep 24 2026 StockStory piece carried by Yahoo noting AMSC fell with JELD-WEN, Shoals, Advanced Energy and Bloom Energy on rebounding energy prices and pressure on growth-dependent names. Sep 24 close 30.42, down 2.03 pct.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and mix, plus acquisition. Q1 FY26 grid revenue rose 27 pct and wind 45 pct on more ECS shipments, with growth including Comtrafo. Gross margin fell to 26.3 pct from roughly 33.8 pct on unfavorable product mix, about 160 bps of Comtrafo purchase accounting and a Brazil direct labor ramp. Management guides second-half margin improvement and says the Q1 mix will not repeat.
web_suppliers: Not disclosed by name. The 10-Q risk factor states we rely upon third-party suppliers for the components and subassemblies of many of our Grid and Wind products, making us vulnerable to supply shortages and price fluctuations. Implied inputs are transformers, capacitor banks, shunt reactors, switchgear and power semiconductors. Comtrafo added three Brazil transformer factories.
web_customers: Concentrated. Inox Wind Limited was 19 pct of total revenue in Q1 FY26 in the wind segment, versus 21 pct a year earlier. Fuji Bridex Pte Ltd was under 10 pct in grid, versus 16 pct a year earlier. The 10-Q states a significant portion of Wind segment revenues derives from a single customer. Management cites a couple dozen key customers.
web_who_loses: Incumbent grid-equipment and power-quality vendors that sell piece parts: large electrical equipment makers such as Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy, GE Vernova, Eaton and S and C, plus standalone capacitor, reactor and STATCOM suppliers and other transformer makers. Also diesel or gas genset suppliers at remote mines whose load grid power replaces through bundled turnkey projects.
web_contradicting_evidence: Stock fell 50.4 pct over 52 weeks and about 33 pct in 63 days despite record revenue and backlog. Q1 non-GAAP net income fell to 7.6M from 11.6M and GAAP net income included an 8.1M non-cash contingent-consideration gain. Q2 GAAP net income is guided to only about 1M. Q1 revenue was pulled forward from Q2. Shares outstanding rose 18.1 pct year on year.
web_if_management_right: Backlog above 400M converts, Q2 revenue beats 85M, second-half gross margin improves, more bundled turnkey orders lift content per project about fivefold, Brazil and Latin America scale, and data center plus AI grid demand adds. Analysts average a 61.75 target. Consensus FY2027 revenue is about 368M, up roughly 23 pct year on year.
web_if_management_wrong: Lumpy orders slip because mining and utility capex depends on customer decisions, leaving Q2 and Q3 short after the Q1 pull-forward. Gross margin stays near 26 pct, non-GAAP profit compresses, Brazil integration and the Comtrafo earnout of up to 382.5 million reais drag, receivables and inventory build, and 176.7M of goodwill is at impairment risk.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Suppliers of capacitor banks, shunt reactors, transformers, switchgear, electrical steel, copper and power semiconductors; engineering procurement and construction contractors who bundle AMSC equipment; the Brazilian transformer supply chain; mining and semiconductor developers whose grid connections get enabled; utilities; naval shipbuilders; wind licensee Inox Wind; data center developers needing power conditioning.
